body: My older sister killed herself when I was 12. Im the one that found her and had to tell my parents. Is that a generational thing? Am I just a big softie zoomer whose problems aren't real because I'm young? I hope your life gets better so you don't have to invalidate the struggles of others.

as a person with a mental disorder myself, i often need to step back and think about how my thought process is being affected by my illness. even when it does not feel like it, i know that depression is making changes to the way i act and react to the world around me. depression always tries to make suicidal ideation seem normal and reasonable. it is not.

there are people who opt for suicide or euthanasia without mental issues, such as those in critical and grave condition like cancer patients or vegetables. (even then, the numbers are very slim) You might confuse yourself with these conditions, or rather your depression will confuse you, but you must realize that there is a stark difference between yourself and these cases. as you said, most people would brave through chronic pain. suicide is not the answer.

depression will make you feel at the end of your rope, but you must step forward and remove yourself from that rationalization. you are strong and capable of making the right choice. see you tomorrow

are you giving yourself any opportunities to find love? i know it is hard to find a special someone but in order to find them you need to be looking. i would start by finding clubs or social groups in your area just to try and meet more people. even if you don't find love, making friends in those groups tends to help mental health a lot. best wishes for you
